---
title: "Story"
---

How do Americans view their leaders, and how does public sentiment toward the White House compare to attitudes toward Congress and political parties? By analyzing monthly Gallup polling data from 1945 to 2026, we can track how public approval, congressional approval, and party favorability interact across various presidential administrations.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10

library(tidyverse)

# Load monthly presidential approval data (1945–2026)
monthly_data <- read_csv("data/presidential_approval_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Load congressional approval data (1974–2025)
congress_data <- read_csv("data/congressional_approval_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Load party favorability data (1992–2025)
party_data <- read_csv("data/party_favorability_by_month.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Single time series styled with clean Axios aesthetic
ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "#D0D0D0", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = monthly_data, aes(x = year_month, y = approval, color = "Public Approval", group = president), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = congress_data, aes(x = year_month, y = approval, color = "Congressional Approval"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = party_data, aes(x = year_month, y = favorability, color = "Party Favorability"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Public Approval" = "#2E74C0",
      "Congressional Approval" = "#8338EC",
      "Party Favorability" = "#2E7D32"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(10, 90, by = 10),
    labels = \(y) paste0(y, "%"),
    limits = c(5, 95)
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "10 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Public, Congressional, and Party Ratings (1945-2026)",
    subtitle = "Monthly Gallup ratings for Presidential Approval (from 1945), Congressional Approval (from 1974),\nand Party Favorability (from 1992). The dashed line marks the 50% threshold.",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Gallup Polls via DataCamp, American Presidency Project, & Gallup Historical Trends"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1a1a1a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#555555", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "lines"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#ECECEC", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "#CCCCCC", linewidth = 0.6),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "#CCCCCC", linewidth = 0.6),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#555555", size = 10),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#888888", size = 8, margin = margin(t = 12))
  )
```

### Key Patterns

- **Presidential Approval:** Typically starts highest during an administration's early months, with notable surges during major national crises (such as late 2001) before trending toward polarized ranges.
- **Congressional Approval:** Stays consistently below presidential ratings and regularly sits below 30%, reflecting longstanding public dissatisfaction with the legislative branch regardless of party control.
- **Party Favorability:** Closely tracks broader partisan dynamics, showing increasing polarization and lower favorability over recent decades.

---

## About

This project was developed for a deeper and more thorough examination of approval ratings and how they evolve over time. It examines historical trends in American political sentiment using monthly polling series from Gallup.

- **Data Sources:** 
  - Presidential job approval ratings (1945–2026) via Gallup and the American Presidency Project.
  - Congressional job approval ratings (1974–2025) via Gallup Historical Trends. *Note: some graphs may not include congressional approval data prior to 1974 due to limited availability.*
  - Party favorability ratings (1992–2025) via Gallup. *Note: some graphs may not include party favorability data prior to 1992 due to limited availability.*
- **Interactive Exploration:** To view individual administration trends with month-by-month animations from Harry Truman to Donald Trump (Second Term), visit the [Exploration](exploration.qmd) page.
